title: Robustness of Persistent Topological Features and Minimum Homological Cuts
summary: Persistent homology is a popular method for computing topological features of (metric) data. Standard approaches based on the Čech or Rips filtration are stable under small perturbations of the data, but highly sensitive to outliers. This lack of robustness has been frequently addressed in the literature. In this paper, we take a novel perspective by asking the following question: When can we guarantee that an observed persistent feature (a bar) is inherent to the underlying data in the presence of a limited number of unknown, arbitrary outliers.
